prs.title: feat(vite-server): handle relative `$fetch` paths in-process with req context
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 📚 Description previously, relative `$fetch` calls on the vite server had no origin to resolve against, so they couldn't reach the app. this change sends relative paths directly to the app handler, in-process, and also passes the context of the request event that made the call as an internal third argument. > [!NOTE] > redirects are not followed

prs.title: fix(nuxt): do not forward the range header to request fetch subrequests
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

### 📚 Description

if a page request carries a `Range` header (for example `Range: bytes=0-10`), `useRequestFetch()` and server-side `useFetch` with a relative URL forward it to the internal API request, meaning an API that honours it can respond with a partial `206` body and the page renders broken data.

this adds `range` to the headers we don't forward, alongside the conditional `if-*` headers which are already excluded.

prs.title: refactor(vite): clean up and simplify
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description this PR mostly removes code that was duplicated in multiple places in the vite builder first, the length-prefixed socket framing was implemented twice, once in the vite-node socket server and once in the client in `vite-node.ts`. both now use utils from `utils/ipc.ts` second, `ModulePreloadPolyfillPlugin` and `TypeCheckPlugin` were the same "prepend an import to the client entry" plugin. they now share `ClientEntryImportPlugin`. we'll need to rebase https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/36918 after merge third, `getTranspilePatterns` and `getTranspileStrings` now share a single resolver for `build.transpile`. fourth, we can share a single "is this a vite route" check for the dev handler and for `cors`. and finally, there are a few other leftovers: unused `hideOutput` logger option and `withLogs` `enabled` flag, the repeated lazy `@vitejs/plugin-vue-jsx` hook forwarding, and the single-use `css.ts` and `types.ts` modules. I've also cleaned up test cases with `it.each`, and merge some of the test cases...

prs.title: refactor(nuxt): split core setup into feature files and share core helpers
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description this tidies up `initNuxt` which was about 1k lines, into feature files to make things a bit clearer: | file | what lives there | | --- | --- | | `builtins.ts` | built-in app plugins and templates (before modules, after modules, after the server build is configured) | | `build-plugins.ts` | core bundler plugins | | `typescript.ts` | tsconfig and type template setup | | `debug-module-mutation.ts` | the `debug` tracking of options mutated by modules | | `modules.ts` / `plugins/import-protection.ts` | module resolution and import protection patterns | alongside that, a few smaller simplifications: - we now share a single implementation for client and server plugin templates and plugin capability probes - we share one event filter for the chokidar watchers - the keyed function plugins simplify the handlers/import path resolution - the perf profiler is simplified + drops some unreachable code - inline single-use build hash options, and drop a few unused internal options and arguments I've also cleaned up the test suite, preferring `it.each` where possible

prs.title: fix(nitro): copy island head arrays before merging entries
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 📚 Description thanks to @DicksonWu654 for reporting this ❤️ if a server component passes a shared array to `useHead` (say, an imported `siteMeta`) and then adds another entry under the same key later in the same render, the later entries end up pushed into the app's own array. they then show up in every later render that uses that array, and the array keeps growing. ```ts import { siteMeta } from '~/utils/site-head' useHead({ meta: siteMeta }) useHead({ meta: [{ name: 'csrf-token', content: perRequestToken }] }) // next visitor's island head now includes this visitor's csrf-token ``` this PR moves the merge into a `mergeIslandHead` helper and copies an array the first time it is stored for a key.

prs.title: fix(nuxt): drop static page meta overridden by runtime value
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description with `experimental.scanPageMeta` and serializable extraction, a `definePageMeta` key whose last occurrence is resolved at runtime keeps the earlier static value in the route record: ```ts definePageMeta({ title: 'static', title: someVar }) definePageMeta({ layout: 'dark', layout: { name: someVar } }) ``` this drops that entry, marking the key dynamic when it is an extraction key.

prs.title: fix(kit): only skip build: false plugins outside development
prs.author: Ice-Hazymoon
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue none ### 📚 Description `build: false` on `addVitePlugin`, `extendViteConfig`, the webpack/rspack helpers and `extendRsbuildConfig` is documented as "Install plugin on build", but the check compares against `nuxt.options.build`, which is the build config object and always truthy. So `build: false` drops the plugin in dev too: it is never installed. I ran into this registering a dev-only Vite plugin from a module with `addVitePlugin(plugin, { build: false })`; nothing ran under `nuxt dev`. This checks `!nuxt.options.dev` instead, the mirror of `dev: false`. The kit test mock had `build: false` in `options`, which hid it; it now uses an object like a real instance, with tests for both options in dev and build. Behaviour change: a module that passes `build: false` today will get its plugin in dev, which is what the option says. The check has been like this since kit was split out (d68318f9d, 2021) and I couldn't find many users of the option.

prs.title: fix(nuxt): warn on duplicate page route names
prs.author: jacobslunga
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue Fixes #36914 ### 📚 Description When multiple pages define the same route name, Nuxt doesn't warn about this collision. This can lead to confusing 404 errors that don't explain the actual problem. This adds a new diagnostic (`NUXT_B4028`) that detects duplicate route names during page resolution and reports the conflicting files. It only warns when at least one route has an explicitly defined name, to avoid false postivies from generated routes. I added tests in `pages.test.ts` covering explicitly named routes, collisions with generated names and nested routes. These tests pass with the fix

prs.title: fix(nuxt): don't retain nuxt instance via global `defineNuxtSchema`
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

resolves #36925

### 📚 Description

the schema module sets `globalThis.defineNuxtSchema` to an arrow function created inside its `setup(_, nuxt)`. that arrow shares `setup`'s closure context, so the global keeps the most recent Nuxt instance alive after it's closed.

this PR moves the identity function to module scope. it also adds a test that loads and closes Nuxt, then checks the instance can be garbage collected. the test only checks the second instance for now, because nitro's global `defineNitroConfig` holds on to the first one, which needs a fix in nitro (https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro-v2/pull/37)
